purpose: Industry roadmap backlog item 3: budget/deadline instrumentation, allocation-failure harnesses, and the worker isolation boundary
scope: Contract headers, one test-binary allocation-failure injector, failure-semantics fixes at the API boundary and in node materialization, and unit/concurrency tests. Not engine consumption of the contracts, not a worker-kill demonstration, and not closure of IR-20/21.
worktree: uncommitted working tree; results identify this state, not HEAD

builds.name: release
builds.command: cmake -S . -B build_contracts -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build_contracts --parallel 12 && ctest --test-dir build_contracts --output-on-failure --timeout 180

builds.name: asan_ubsan_warnings_as_errors
builds.command: cmake -S . -B build_asan_contracts -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DMARKOV_CERO_ENABLE_ASAN_UBSAN=ON -DMARKOV_CERO_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON && cmake --build build_asan_contracts --parallel 12 && ctest --test-dir build_asan_contracts --output-on-failure --timeout 300

builds.name: tsan_warnings_as_errors
builds.command: cmake -S . -B build_tsan_contracts -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DMARKOV_CERO_ENABLE_TSAN=ON -DMARKOV_CERO_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON && cmake --build build_tsan_contracts --parallel 12 && ctest --test-dir build_tsan_contracts --output-on-failure --timeout 600

allocation_failure_harness.implementation: tests/support/failing_new.hpp replaces global operator new/delete in the resource_failure_test binary; arm(nth) makes exactly the nth subsequent allocation fail (std::bad_alloc, nullptr for nothrow forms) and counting continues past it so unwinding stays safe
allocation_failure_harness.gtest_free: tests are plain main() programs using a throwing require() helper, consistent with the rest of the suite

assertions: no exception escapes solve_file or solve_model
an injected failure is never reported as infeasible or unbounded
at least one injected failure is reported as resource_limit with failure_site allocation_failure
the harness reaches the target path (injection actually occurred)

diagnostic_driver.note: A separate, non-CTest driver over the same harness, run from the repository root; recorded here as supporting evidence for the boundary claim.

contract_paths: ModelSnapshot::capture: throws std::bad_alloc on an injected failure, stays deterministic and fingerprint-stable after disarm
NodeView::materialize: returns MaterializationStatus::allocation_failed, charged_bytes 0, budget released, budget not marked exhausted, output contents untouched
budget refusal remains distinct: MaterializationStatus::budget_exhausted with sticky exhaustion

failure_semantics_fixes: src/api/api.cpp: guarded() catches std::bad_alloc before the generic std::exception handler (previously reported numerical_failure) and both solve_file and solve_model wrap their whole body so allocation failure cannot escape the API
include/markov_cero/milp/node_view.hpp + src/milp/node_view.cpp: new MaterializationStatus::allocation_failed separates host allocation failure from solve-budget exhaustion
include/markov_cero/milp/node_bounds.hpp: NodeBounds::materialize builds its delta path (its last allocation) before writing outputs, so an allocation failure cannot leave a half-written result

instrumentation_contract.stage_scope: include/markov_cero/core/instrumentation.hpp: exactly one TraceEvent per stage scope (early return and unwinding included) with stage name, shared sticky stop reason, stage counter, net charged bytes during the stage, observed elapsed_ms and worker index
instrumentation_contract.deadline: SolveContext::remaining_ms() reports live slack (empty when untimed, 0 once expired); enforcement stays cooperative through poll()
instrumentation_contract.trace_event: TraceEvent.worker added (0 = solve-level) so parallel stages are distinguishable

private: release rights clamped to what the worker charged
worker_isolation_boundary.failure_semantics: a refused charge marks the shared budget exhausted and records the solve-wide memory_budget_exhausted stop, also stops the requesting worker; destruction returns held bytes; attribution overflow fails closed instead of wrapping
worker_isolation_boundary.coverage: tests/worker_context_test.cpp: local-stop isolation, attribution and clamped release, shared exhaustion stopping every worker, attribution overflow, worker-tagged events, and a four-thread concurrent charge/release run against one shared budget

python.note: The boundary classification change (bad_alloc -> resource_limit) is C++ only; the Python result dict is unchanged by this slice.

static_checks.source_limits: python3 scripts/check_source_limits.py -> 443 maintained files, maximum 300 lines, 0 violations
static_checks.doc_links: python3 scripts/check_docs.py -> 8 active documents checked, 0 broken local links

limitations: Instrumentation and the worker boundary are contracts with tests only: no engine stage constructs a StageScope, the API boundary does not create a SolveContext, SolveOptions still exposes no solve-wide time or memory limit, and the parallel tree search does not use WorkerContext. That consumption work is backlog item 5.

Allocation-failure coverage is bounded: the CTest gate injects at the first 16 model and 8 file allocation points, the diagnostic driver at 200 and 24. Other engines (QP, PDLP, MILP, parallel, NLP/MINLP), proof and verification stages, and allocations made on worker threads were not systematically covered.

Engine- and verifier-internal generic catch (const std::exception&) handlers can in principle reclassify a host allocation failure as a numerical or fallback outcome; none was observed at the injected points, which is not a proof that none exists on other paths.

The injector is a test-binary-only global operator new/delete replacement; production code has no allocation-failure simulation, no emergency reserve, and no allocation-failure recovery path beyond the boundary mapping.

GCC's dead-allocation elimination can remove naive allocation probes, so the harness self-check pins pointers through an asm barrier; future tests that probe allocations directly must do the same or they will silently test nothing.
No worker kill/recovery demonstration, no OS-level memory or time limits, no process isolation, and no peak-RSS measurement accompany the boundary definition (all remain W02 acceptance items).
No deadline or cancellation latency measurement is included; remaining_ms() reports slack but nothing yet enforces a deadline through the new context.
The TSan run covers the current suite only; it cannot exercise WorkerContext inside the parallel search because that wiring does not exist yet.
Python results were exercised on one local interpreter (3.14) and one host; other interpreters and platforms remain untested here.
